title: Efficient Lindbladian Learning from Constant-Time Pauli Responses
authors: Jiaxing Song, Yukun Zhang, Xiao Yuan, Yusen Wu
abstract: Learning the generator of an open many-body system is more challenging than Hamiltonian learning: local responses, which can directly reveal coherent interaction terms in closed-system dynamics, may also contain dissipative contributions in open-system dynamics. In this paper, we address this challenge by developing an efficient Lindbladian learning framework for a known local candidate generator dictionary with bounded dissipative support and either bounded dual-interaction-graph degree or bounded unweighted local strength. The framework resolves the coherent-dissipative ambiguity by treating local Pauli responses as a linear system over both types of generator terms. Inverting this response system separates their contributions and makes the individual Lindbladian coefficients accessible from local response data in a fixed short-time window. Within this framework, we develop two efficient learning algorithms: Chebyshev--Lobatto response interpolation, which uses logarithmically many short evolution times and has a post-mean cost linear in $M$, with the stated dependence on $ε$, and Single-time projected response contraction, which uses a single fixed evolution time and globally inverts a truncated response function. Both procedures estimate $M$ candidate coefficients to entrywise accuracy $ε$ using $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(M/ε^2)$ sample and classical post-processing complexity. Our theoretical results establish local response inversion as a scalable paradigm for learning, calibrating, and diagnosing complex quantum systems from experimentally accessible short-time data.
summary: This paper presents an advanced framework to learn the generator (Lindbladian) of complex open quantum systems using only short-time local Pauli response measurements. It resolves the inherent difficulty of separating coherent and dissipative dynamics by treating responses as a linear system. The authors propose two efficient, theoretically bounded algorithms—Chebyshev interpolation and single-time contraction—to extract all necessary coupling coefficients from experimental data.
main_problem: The core challenge is efficiently learning the generator (Lindbladian) of an open many-body quantum system, which is complicated by dissipative contributions mixed into local Pauli response measurements.
main_result: The authors develop and analyze two efficient algorithms—Chebyshev–Lobatto interpolation and single-time projected contraction—to separate coherent and dissipative terms and estimate all Lindbladian coefficients from short-time data with provable complexity bounds.
method: The approach involves constructing a linear system from raw Pauli responses, inverting it to isolate the contribution of each generator term, and then applying advanced numerical interpolation or iterative projection techniques to extract the time-dependent coefficients.
model_or_system: The study concerns open quantum systems governed by Lindbladian dynamics ($\mathcal{L}^\dagger_	heta$). Learning relies on measuring local Pauli responses from randomized product-Pauli experiments, which provide data related to the system's evolution operator $e^{\mathcal{L}^\dagger t}$.
key_observables: Local Pauli response functionals $	ext{Tr}[ho P(t)]$, normalized finite-time responses $g_\alpha(t, 	heta)$, and the unknown Lindbladian coefficients $	heta = (	heta_1, \dots, 	heta_M)^T$.
important_parameters: Target accuracy ($\epsilon$), number of candidate terms ($M$), evolution time window ($t$), and system locality scales ($\Lambda$).
main_assumptions: The dictionary of candidate Lindbladian terms must be known; the dissipative part must satisfy bounded locality properties (e.g., bounded dual-interaction-graph degree).
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates a three-stage process: (a) measuring raw responses via Pauli experiments, (b) normalizing these responses by inverting a response matrix ($H=G^{-1}$) to separate coherent/dissipative mixing, and (c) reconstructing the coefficients using interpolation or single-time inversion.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical problem of Lindbladian learning from local responses. It then details the mathematical framework involving response matrices ($G$ and $H$) to resolve ambiguities. Finally, it presents two distinct algorithmic approaches (Chebyshev interpolation and single-time contraction) alongside rigorous complexity analyses for both measurement shots and classical post-processing.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly systematic and theoretically grounded methodology for extracting fundamental system parameters from limited, noisy experimental data in open quantum systems. The explicit handling of the coherent-dissipative ambiguity is crucial for interpreting measurements in realistic physical platforms like superconducting circuits or trapped ions.
